donor_source.author: Kless Gyzen
donor_source.review_boundary: weathered-rock morphology analog only; no exact South Fork lithology claim and no production promotion without geology, guide, art, and performance review

pixel_delta_from_v189.note: These whole-frame deltas include temporal water and lighting differences. The extremely small changed-pixel coverage confirms that the existing instance scales and placements prevent the scan donors from producing a meaningful full-reach bank change; the values are not a quality score.

accepted_improvements: The six scan donors create more varied and natural silhouettes than the single repeated procedural boulder where large scenic-rock instances are visible at Meat Grinder and Troublemaker.
The opt-in review proves a reversible, package-safe comparison path for evaluating already-rights-reviewed static-mesh donors across the complete settled map.
rejection_reasons: The swap changes only 0.047960% to 0.160482% of pixels above an eight-level RGB threshold across the five fixed views, so it is not a meaningful full-reach visual upgrade.
Existing shore-cobble instance scales reduce metre-scale donor meshes to small, mostly invisible fragments at guide-eye distance.
Chili Bar, Coloma, and Salmon Falls retain broad flat painted banks with almost no legible embedded-rock or gravel-bar structure.
The visible Meat Grinder and Troublemaker boulders do not supply cutbanks, bar relief, roots, undercut edges, or a credible wet shoreline transition.
Repeated vegetation, low-frequency terrain, broad water, lighting, and sparse scene dressing remain visibly synthetic.
No named art, guide, geology, geospatial, owner, performance, or rights reviewer approved the candidate.
manual_review.review_asset_retention: retain the imported CC0 review assets, captures, provenance, and opt-in transient comparison path; do not replace production meshes or alter collision authority
manual_review.next_required_work: author source-conditioned bank-form geometry with metre-scale cutbanks and gravel bars, embedded-rock distributions sized for guide-eye visibility, and a material-aware wet-edge transition before another five-view comparison
